title: Evidence and release contract
description: Adds compact committed JSON evidence with requirement proofs and script-driven release versioning.

acceptance: Patch IDs use UTC YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS and a one-to-three-word slug.
Evidence directories are grouped by the last published baseline tag.
Evidence commits contain exactly manifest.json and evidence.json.
The manifest copy is byte-identical to the patch-pack manifest.
Evidence does not contain its own evidence commit SHA or repeat manifest commands and expected scope.
Every manifest requirement appears exactly once in evidence.
Passing requirements include verifiable implementation-commit proofs.
Text proofs validate path, inclusive lines, snippet SHA-256, and optional symbol.
JSON pointer and deletion proofs are supported.
Gate definitions and commands live only in manifest.json.
Evidence records compact results by gate ID.
Every required gate appears exactly once and passes.
Deviations are stored inside evidence.json.
Accepted deviations cannot claim changed behavior; only an explicitly owner-approved manifest-correction deviation may claim changed scope.
Markdown deviation templates are removed.
The evidence commit directly follows the implementation commit.
Prepare and committed modes validate exact two-file evidence scope.
The checker does not rerun project quality gates.
The old long-name evidence directory is deleted.
No legacy manifest is reconstructed or migrated.
VERSION is canonical.
Configured plain, JSON, and TOML version fields are synchronized through scripts/release.py.
Release preparation, commit, tag, and tag verification are separate explicit operations.
README contains no concrete current semantic version.
README installation and release examples use generic immutable tag placeholders.
CI checks version consistency and tag identity.
Patch and evidence JSON schemas are present.
Patch generation and validation understand requirements, gates, and pending evidence templates.
Dependency-free tests cover evidence proofs and release automation.

gpt_static_checks_performed: reviewed current main, merged PR metadata, README, VERSION, workflows, schemas, templates, and patch generator
designed compact JSON evidence with requirement proofs, gate IDs, structured deviations, and two-commit verification
prepared release automation, schemas, tests, documentation, self-contained applicator, and pack verifier
performed static syntax, JSON, declared-scope, and archive-integrity checks only
known_integration_risks: The release script rewrites configured JSON version files using stable two-space formatting.
TOML version updates require an explicitly configured table and key.
The obsolete evidence files are intentionally deleted; their prior contents remain available in Git history.
GitHub Release publication is exercised only after an explicit validated tag push.
forbidden_deviations: Do not change VERSION; it must remain 1.0.1 in the implementation commit.
Do not create or push a tag, merge a pull request, or publish a Release without owner approval.
Do not add a concrete current project version to README.md.
Do not create Markdown AGENT_RESULT or DEVIATIONS evidence files.
Do not add evidence_commit, patch identity, commands, or expected scope to evidence.json.
Do not weaken exact implementation scope, proof hash, gate completeness, or evidence diff verification.
